mainTopic: The end of the רב–שמואל discussion about a שומרת יבם; a man who married a chain of half-sisters after false death reports; and the power of a nine-year-old יבם's ביאה, מאמר and גט
overview: The גמרא finishes settling an apparent contradiction in שמואל's views. It offers several answers. Maybe שמואל agreed with רבי יוסי only on one point. Or maybe the dispute between רב and שמואל about a שומרת יבם being 'like an אשת איש' is about רב המנונא's rule on זנות, or about whether an outsider's קידושין take effect with her. Then a new משנה presents a man who heard false reports that his wife died and married her half-sisters one after another. It rules which of the women are his valid wives, and it explains how the answer flips if the first wife really did die. A second משנה teaches that a nine-year-old יבם and his adult brothers can each block the other from the יבמה. The גמרא works out that the boy's ביאה blocks his brothers even when it comes last, while his מאמר blocks only when it comes first. Finally, sources show that the boy also has a גט and a מאמר, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the boy's גט is real but weaker than an adult's.

steps.title: Maybe שמואל agreed only with the 'does not disqualify' ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that when שמואל ruled like רבי יוסי, he meant only the part of the case where the man 'does not disqualify.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe שמואל's agreement with רבי יוסי refers only to the ruling 'he does not disqualify'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction it raised just before this point. It suggests that שמואל agreed with רבי יוסי on only one specific point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction came from assuming that שמואל's 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי' covered everything רבי יוסי said. The גמרא narrows it: שמואל may have meant only the ruling that 'he does not disqualify' (the case where his wife and brother-in-law went away). Once the agreement is narrowed, it no longer clashes with שמואל's other view.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a possible alternative reading)
He does not disqualify (does not make her forbidden)

phrases.english: But perhaps [שמואל's ruling refers] to 'he does not disqualify'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא אַ״אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised just before this section against שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's agreement with רבי יוסי covered his entire ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל agreed only with the 'does not disqualify' part, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Another answer: drop רב הונא's explanation and use רב המנונא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way out. Perhaps רב הונא's explanation of the dispute is not accepted at all, and רב and שמואל are really arguing about רב המנונא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: how do we know that רב הונא's explanation is correct? Maybe it is not correct at all, and they are arguing about רב המנונא's rule. רב המנונא said: a שומרת יבם who committed זנות is forbidden to her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a completely different answer. It throws out the assumption, based on רב הונא, that created the contradiction. It then introduces רב המנונא's rule as the new topic of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only existed because the גמרא read the רב–שמואל dispute the way רב הונא explained it. If we drop רב הונא's reading, the dispute can be about something else: whether a woman waiting for יבום becomes forbidden to her יבם through זנות. רב המנונא says she does, and the next step shows how רב and שמואל line up on this.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her brother-in-law to do יבום or חליצה

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: מִמַּאי דְּאִיתַהּ לִדְרַב הוּנָא?
phrases.english: Alternatively: from where [do we know] that רב הונא's [explanation] holds?
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's explanation of the argument between רב and שמואל, which the גמרא used to set up the contradiction.

phrases.english: Perhaps רב הונא's [explanation] does not hold at all,
and they are arguing about רב המנונא's [rule].
For רב המנונא said:
A woman waiting for her יבם who committed זנות —
is forbidden to her יבם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: מִמַּאי דְּאִיתַהּ לִדְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל's dispute must be explained the way רב הונא explained it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their dispute could instead be about רב המנונא's rule, so no contradiction arises.

steps.title: How רב and שמואל line up on רב המנונא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב holds she is like an אשת איש and so becomes disqualified through זנות. שמואל holds she is not like an אשת איש and is not disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said she is like a married woman, so she becomes disqualified through זנות. שמואל said she is not like a married woman, so she does not become disqualified through זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the new reading of the dispute. It shows how the words 'like an אשת איש' fit onto רב המנונא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real married woman who commits זנות becomes forbidden to her husband. רב treats the שומרת יבם the same way, so זנות forbids her to the יבם, which agrees with רב המנונא. שמואל says she is not truly like a married woman, so זנות does not forbid her to the יבם.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: For רב said: she is like a married woman,
and she is disqualified through זנות.
And שמואל said: she is not like a married woman,
and she is not disqualified through זנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the dispute according to the answer given in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב she is forbidden to the יבם after זנות, as an אשת איש would be to her husband. According to שמואל she is not.

steps.title: A third option: they argue whether קידושין take effect with a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another possible topic for the dispute: whether another man's קידושין take effect with a woman waiting for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else they are arguing about whether קידושין take effect with a יבמה. רב said she is like a married woman, so קידושין do not take effect with her. שמואל said she is not like a married woman, so קידושין do take effect with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives yet another way to understand 'like an אשת איש.' Here it is about whether an outside man can marry her before יבום or חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one else can betroth a married woman. רב says the יבמה is the same, so an outsider's קידושין are void. שמואל says she is not a full married woman, so the outsider's קידושין do take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A widow bound to her husband's brother for יבום

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי נָמֵי, בְּקִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בִּיבָמָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: And alternatively, they are arguing about whether קידושין take effect with a יבמה,
phrases.notes: This means קידושין from some other man, not from the יבם himself.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: for רב said: she is like a married woman,
and קידושין do not take effect with her.
And שמואל said: she is not like a married woman,
and קידושין do take effect with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי, בְּקִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בִּיבָמָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another possible topic for the dispute, in place of רב המנונא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the subject of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute must be about רב הונא's explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute could be about whether קידושין take effect with a יבמה.

steps.title: But they already argued about that once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer, because רב and שמואל already disagreed elsewhere about קידושין with a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this one time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the third option from step 4. Why would the same dispute be recorded twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, רב and שמואל are already recorded arguing about whether קידושין take effect with a יבמה. If this dispute is about the same point, it seems to be a pointless repeat. The גמרא assumes a dispute would not be recorded twice for no reason.

phrases.english: But they already disagreed about it one time?
phrases.notes: Meaning רב and שמואל already have a recorded argument over whether קידושין take effect with a יבמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִפְּלִיגוּ בַּהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the dispute is about קידושין with a יבמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same dispute between the same אמוראים would not be recorded twice for no reason.

steps.title: One dispute was inferred from the other
steps.stepSummary: Only one of the two disputes was actually said. The other was worked out from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was stated by inference from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. There really was only one dispute; the second record was drawn out of the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל did not argue twice. One version is what they actually said. The other version was learned from it by inference, so the double record is not a pointless repeat. This saves the answer from step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, from the implication of

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to read 'she is like an אשת איש' in the dispute between רב and שמואל: רב הונא's explanation, רב המנונא's rule about זנות, or whether קידושין take effect. The double record of the קידושין dispute is explained by one being inferred from the other.

phrases.english: One was stated by inference from the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מִכְּלָל דַּחֲבֶרְתַּהּ אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They argued twice about the same thing, which would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argued only once; the second record was inferred from the first.

steps.title: New משנה: a man who married a chain of half-sisters after false death reports
steps.stepSummary: A man is told four times that his wife died. Each time he marries her half-sister, alternating between a sister from the father's side and one from the mother's side. All five turn out to be alive, and he may stay with the first, third and fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him, 'Your wife died,' and he married her sister from her father. She 'died,' and he married her sister from her mother. She 'died,' and he married her sister from her father. She 'died,' and he married her sister from her mother. Then they were all found alive. He is permitted to the first, the third and the fifth, and they exempt their צרות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a tricky case of false reports of death. The man ends up with five women, each a half-sister of the one before her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sisters alternate between the father's side and the mother's side. So the first, third and fifth are not sisters of each other, and his marriages to them are valid. The second and fourth were sisters of a living wife, so those marriages were never valid. Because the first, third and fifth are real wives, if he dies, יבום with one of them exempts the other wives (her צרות).

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
Her sister from her father (paternal half-sister)
Her sister from her mother (maternal half-sister)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume all five women are forbidden just because they are a chain of sisters. Each woman is a sister only of the women right next to her in the chain, so the first, third and fifth are unrelated to each other.

phrases.english: משנה: They said to him: 'Your wife died,'
and he married her sister from her father.
[They told him] she died, and he married her sister from her mother.
She died, and he married her sister from her father.
She died, and he married her sister from her mother,
and they were all found to be alive —
he is permitted to the first, the third and the fifth,
and they exempt their co-wives.
phrases.notes: If he dies, יבום or חליצה with one of these real wives exempts the other wives from יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמְרוּ לוֹ: ״מֵתָה אִשְׁתְּךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unconnected to the preceding discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a chain of false death reports in which he married alternating paternal and maternal half-sisters, the man may stay with the first, third and fifth wives, and they exempt their צרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that being forbidden as a wife's sister depends on the actual family link between two specific women, not on being part of a chain.

steps.title: The second and fourth sisters are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The man is forbidden to the second and fourth women. If his brother does יבום with one of them, it does not exempt her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is forbidden to the second and the fourth wife. If his brother has relations with one of them, that does not exempt her co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling from the previous step continues. It now gives the other side: which of the five women he is NOT allowed to stay with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first wife was really alive the whole time, so the second wife was her sister. That makes the second an אחות אשה, and the marriage never took effect. The fourth is the sister of the valid third wife, so the same problem applies. Since these were forbidden relations for the husband, his brother's ביאה with one of them is not a real יבום, and it cannot free her צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: relations (here, the brother's act of יבום)
co-wife (another wife of the same husband)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'relations' here are not the husband's. They are the brother's, after the husband dies. The question is whether that act counts as יבום that frees the other wife.

phrases.english: And he is forbidden to the second and the fourth,
and the relations with any one of them
phrases.notes: This means the brother's relations after the husband dies, when he comes to do יבום.

phrases.english: do not exempt her co-wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָסוּר בַּשְּׁנִיָּה וּבָרְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of step 7 by naming the forbidden wives and what that means for יבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second and fourth wives are forbidden to him. A brother's relations with one of them do not exempt her צרה.

steps.title: A second version: the first wife really died
steps.stepSummary: If the first wife really died before he married the second, everything flips. The second and fourth are permitted and they exempt their צרות. The third and fifth are forbidden and do not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married the second after the first truly died, he is permitted to the second and fourth, and they exempt their co-wives. He is forbidden to the third and fifth, and relations with one of them do not exempt her co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The case is given again with one change. This time the first wife really did die, and only the later reports were false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the second marriage is valid, because her sister is no longer alive. That makes the third (the second's sister) an אחות אשה, so that marriage fails. The fourth is the sister of the third, who is alive but was never validly his wife, so the fourth's marriage is valid. The fifth is the sister of the valid fourth, so she is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Which wives are valid depends on one question: was the wife's sister alive when he married her? If the sister's own marriage was invalid, she does not count as his wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a forbidden relationship (ערוה) for the husband removes the whole יבום. That is why only the valid wives can free their co-wives.

phrases.english: And if he had relations with the second
after the death of the first,
phrases.notes: The first wife really did die this time. Only the later reports turned out false.

phrases.english: he is permitted to the second and the fourth,
and they exempt their co-wives,
and he is forbidden to the third and the fifth,
and the relations with any one of them
do not exempt her co-wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּא עַל הַשְּׁנִיָּה לְאַחַר מִיתַת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the case with the first wife actually dead, which reverses which wives are valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first wife truly died, the second and fourth are valid and exempt their צרות. The third and fifth are forbidden and do not exempt.

steps.title: New משנה: a nine-year-old and his brothers block each other
steps.stepSummary: A boy of nine years and one day who has relations with his יבמה blocks his brothers from her. The brothers also block him. But he blocks only if he acted first, while they block him whether they acted first or last.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy aged nine years and one day disqualifies her from the brothers, and the brothers disqualify her from him. But he disqualifies only if he acted first, while the brothers disqualify whether they acted first or last.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new subject: a young יבם who is old enough for his ביאה to matter, but still a minor. It states the general rule first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy of nine and a day has relations that count for something, but he is not an adult. So his ביאה blocks the other brothers from the יבמה. The block works in both directions, but it is not equal. His act matters only if it comes first. The brothers' act blocks him at any point.

keyTerms.meaning: a boy of nine years and one day
first and last (either before or after)

steps.confusionAlert: 'He disqualifies on the brothers' means his act makes the woman forbidden to them. It does not mean the brothers themselves become disqualified people.

phrases.english: A boy aged nine years and one day:
he disqualifies her from the brothers,
and the brothers disqualify her from him.
But he disqualifies only first,
while the brothers disqualify first and last.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד הוּא פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a different topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-year-old יבם and the adult brothers block each other from the יבמה. He blocks only if he is first, but they block him first or last.

steps.title: How the blocking works in practice
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its rule. If the boy has relations with his יבמה, the brothers are blocked. If the brothers have relations, do מאמר, give a גט, or do חליצה, he is blocked.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A boy of nine years and one day who had relations with his יבמה has disqualified her from the brothers. If the brothers had relations with her, made a מאמר with her, gave a גט, or did חליצה, they disqualify her from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'how so?' and then spells out its general rule with real actions. It lists what each side can do that blocks the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the boy, only one action is listed: ביאה. For the adult brothers, a whole list of actions blocks him: ביאה, מאמר, גט, or חליצה. The 'first and last' in step 10 is a separate point about timing: the brothers' acts block him whether they come before or after his.

keyTerms.meaning: his brother's widow, waiting for יבום
a rabbinic kind of betrothal done with a יבמה

steps.whatToRemember: The boy blocks the brothers only through his own ביאה, and only if he is first. The brothers block him through ביאה, מאמר, גט or חליצה.

phrases.english: How so?
A boy aged nine years and one day
who had relations with his yevama
has disqualified her from the brothers.
If the brothers had relations with her,
or made a levirate betrothal with her,
gave a bill of divorce, or performed ḥalitza,
they disqualify her from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the general rule of step 10 with specific actions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boy's ביאה blocks the brothers. The brothers' ביאה, מאמר, גט, or חליצה blocks him.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'after the first wife died'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה singles out one case as 'after the death of the first,' since every case already started with a report that she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is that to say that all the other cases are not after the death of the first wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה from Step 9. It asks why one case is described as 'after the first wife died,' when every case in the משנה begins with news that she died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each marriage in the משנה happened because the man heard his wife had died. So calling only one case 'after her death' seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what extra point that phrase is making.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that comes after the משנה (written here in short as גְּמָ׳)
Is that to say...? (a question that challenges an assumption)
The death of the first wife

phrases.english: Gemara: Is that to say that all of them
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the other cases in the משנה about the man who married several sisters.

phrases.english: are not after the death of the first one?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's line in Step 9: 'if he had relations with the second after the death of the first.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ לָאו לְאַחַר מִיתַת רִאשׁוֹנָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by questioning the wording of the משנה in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'after the death of the first' in Step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every case already assumes a report that the first wife died, so the phrase seems to add nothing.

steps.title: It means her death was certain
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the משנה means a confirmed death, not just a report.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It means after the certain death of the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. The special case in the משנה is one where we know for sure the first wife died, not only that people reported it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other cases the report was false, because she was alive. In this case she truly died before he married the second sister. That is why the results flip, as Step 9 described.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question

steps.whatToRemember: 'After the death of the first' in the משנה means a confirmed death. The other cases were only false reports.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְאַחַר מִיתַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וַדַּאי.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: After the certain death of the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְאַחַר מִיתַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וַדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the phrase more precisely (a confirmed death versus a reported one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase seemed to repeat what was true in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means the death was certain, which is a different case from a false report.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the boy blocks even when he acts second
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the nine-year-old blocks his brothers only if he acts first. But a ברייתא says that if a brother did מאמר and the boy then had relations with her, the boy blocks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'a boy of nine years,' etc. Does a nine-year-old block only when he is first, and not when he is last? But רב זביד בר רב אושעיא taught: If one does מאמר with his יבמה, and afterward his nine-year-old brother has relations with her, the boy has disqualified her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, about the nine-year-old boy. It challenges the rule 'he blocks only first' with a ברייתא where he blocks even though he came second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the adult brother acted first with מאמר. The boy's relations came after that, and still they blocked her. That seems to contradict the משנה's statement that the boy blocks only when he acts first.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) teach...? (brings a ברייתא as a challenge)
A rabbinic betrothal of the יבמה by a brother, done with words or money

steps.confusionAlert: 'First' and 'last' do not mean first or last in age. They mean whether the boy acted before or after his brother did something with the יבמה.

phrases.english: A boy of nine years, etc.
A boy of nine years and one day:
does he disqualify first, but not disqualify last?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָנֵי רַב זְבִיד בַּר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Zevid bar Rav Oshaya teach:
One who does levirate betrothal with his yevama,
and afterward his brother came

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד עָלֶיהָ — פְּסָלָהּ!
phrases.english: who is nine years and one day old, upon her: he has disqualified her!
phrases.notes: 'Came upon her' means he had relations with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַב זְבִיד בַּר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the nine-year-old part of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the nine-year-old blocks only if he acts first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the boy acting second, after a brother's מאמר, and he still blocks.

steps.title: Relations block even second, מאמר blocks only first
steps.stepSummary: The answer separates the boy's two kinds of acts. His ביאה blocks even when it comes last. His מאמר blocks only when it comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Intercourse disqualifies even last. Levirate betrothal disqualifies first, but last it does not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about different acts by the boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about the boy's ביאה, which is strong enough to block even after a brother's מאמר. The משנה's 'first only' rule would then be about the boy's מאמר, which is weaker.

phrases.english: They say: intercourse disqualifies even last;
levirate betrothal disqualifies first,
but last it does not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: בִּיאָה פָּסֵיל אֲפִילּוּ בְּסוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of act (ביאה versus מאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boy blocks only first, no matter what he does.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boy's ביאה blocks even last. Only his מאמר is limited to blocking first.

steps.title: But the משנה's own example is relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The משנה says the boy blocks only first, and its example of that rule is a boy who had relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does intercourse disqualify even last? But the משנה teaches: 'Except that he disqualifies first, and they disqualify first and last. How so? A boy of nine years and one day who had relations with his yevama,' etc.!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15 using the wording of the משנה itself (Steps 10 and 11).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains its 'first only' rule with the words 'a boy who had relations with his יבמה.' So the 'first only' limit seems to apply to ביאה too. That contradicts the claim that ביאה blocks even last.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches...! (quotes the משנה as a challenge)

phrases.english: And intercourse disqualifies even last?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָתָנֵי: אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא פּוֹסֵל תְּחִלָּה,
phrases.english: But it teaches: except that he disqualifies first,
and they, first and last. How so?
A boy of nine years and one day
who had relations with his yevama, etc.!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִיאָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּסוֹף פָּסֵיל? וְהָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 15 that the boy's ביאה blocks even last
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses ביאה as its example of the 'first only' rule, so ביאה seems limited to first.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה with words added. The 'first only' rule is about מאמר, and the example 'a boy who had relations' shows that his ביאה blocks even last.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: A boy of nine years and one day disqualifies first, and the brothers disqualify first and last. When is this said? With levirate betrothal. But intercourse disqualifies even last. How so? A boy of nine years and one day who had relations with his yevama has disqualified the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the משנה left out a line. With that line restored, the example of relations illustrates a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added line, 'when is this said? With מאמר,' limits the 'first only' rule to מאמר. The example of the boy who had relations now shows that ביאה blocks the brothers even when it comes after their act. This fits the ברייתא of רב זביד.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words (and here is the full version)
And this is what it teaches
In what case are these words said? (limits a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: A nine-year-old's מאמר blocks the brothers only if it comes first. His ביאה blocks them even if it comes after a brother's act. The brothers' acts block him whether they come first or last.
steps.confusionAlert: The example 'a boy who had relations' does not illustrate the 'first only' rule. In the corrected reading, it illustrates the new line that ביאה blocks even last.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the final rule for a nine-year-old: the type of act decides whether its timing matters.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
A boy of nine years and one day:
he disqualifies first,
and they disqualify first and last.
In what case are these words said? With levirate betrothal;
but intercourse disqualifies even last.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיצַד: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: How so? A boy of nine years and one day

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ — פָּסַל עַל יְדֵי אַחִין.
phrases.english: who had relations with his yevama has disqualified the brothers.
phrases.notes: Read this as: he had relations after a brother had already done מאמר, just like the ברייתא in Step 14.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 by restoring missing words in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The משנה is missing words (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's example of relations was illustrating the 'first only' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'First only' applies to מאמר. The example of relations shows that ביאה blocks even last.

steps.title: Does the boy even have מאמר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a nine-year-old's מאמר counts at all. A ברייתא says he blocks his brothers in only one way, through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a nine-year-old even have a מאמר that affects his brothers? A ברייתא teaches that he disqualifies the woman for his brothers in only one way, ביאה. But his brothers disqualify her for him in four ways: ביאה, מאמר, גט and חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the assumption from Step 15 that the boy's מאמר works when it comes first. A ברייתא counts only one act of his that blocks the brothers, and it is not מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 split the boy's acts: his ביאה always blocks, and his מאמר blocks only when it comes first. This ברייתא seems to say his מאמר never blocks, because it names only ביאה. So the whole idea that the boy has a working מאמר is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Levirate betrothal: the יבם betroths the יבמה with money or a document, before the full marriage
Disqualifies, meaning he makes her forbidden to the other brothers
The ceremony that releases the יבמה from the brothers

steps.confusionAlert: Read the two lists carefully. The boy blocks his brothers with one act only (ביאה). The brothers block the boy with four acts. The challenge comes from the short list.

phrases.english: And does he have levirate betrothal at all
phrases.notes: "He" is the nine-year-old boy from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: with regard to the brothers?
But isn't it taught:
A boy aged nine years and one day,
he disqualifies in one way,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאַחִין פּוֹסְלִין עַל יָדוֹ בְּאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים.
phrases.english: and the brothers disqualify with regard to him in four ways.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אַחִין בְּבִיאָה,
phrases.english: He disqualifies with regard to the brothers by relations,
and the brothers disqualify with regard to him
by relations, by levirate betrothal, by a bill of divorce, by חליצה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ מַאֲמָר כְּלָל עַל יְדֵי אַחִין? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind Steps 15 and 17 that the boy's מאמר can block when it comes first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a nine-year-old's מאמר blocks his brothers when it comes first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only ביאה as the boy's blocking act. So it seems his מאמר has no effect at all.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists only rules that have no conditions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא names only ביאה because ביאה blocks in every order. The boy's מאמר depends on order, so the ברייתא could not state it as a flat rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: ביאה blocks whether it comes first or last, so the תנא could state it flatly. מאמר blocks if it comes first but not if it comes last, so he could not state it flatly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא left out מאמר because it only lists acts that always block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boy's ביאה blocks in every case, so it fits a simple list. His מאמר blocks only when it comes first, so listing it would have required adding a condition. Leaving it out does not mean his מאמר has no power.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a clear-cut rule for him, one that can be stated without conditions
At the beginning, meaning before the brother's act
At the end, meaning after the brother's act

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא reads a list: a תנא may leave out a rule because it has conditions, not because the rule doesn't exist.

phrases.english: Relations, which disqualify
whether first or last —
it is definite for him,
phrases.notes: Meaning the תנא can state it as a flat rule with no "if" attached.

phrases.english: levirate betrothal, which disqualifies when first,
but when last does not disqualify —
is not definite for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיאָה דְּפָסְלָה בֵּין בִּתְחִלָּה בֵּין בְּסוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the source left the case out: the ברייתא lists only unconditional rules.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving מאמר out of the boy's list means his מאמר has no effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boy's מאמר does work when it comes first. The ברייתא left it out only because it depends on order.

steps.title: אמוראים confirm the boy has גט and מאמר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from אמוראים. Through רב יהודה, שמואל rules that the boy has a valid גט, and רב תחליפא בר אבימי rules that he has a valid מאמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, the boy has a גט. And רב תחליפא בר אבימי also said: he has a מאמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with rulings of אמוראים: the nine-year-old's גט and מאמר both have legal force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 assumed the boy's מאמר works. Here אמוראים say so directly, and they add that his גט works too. This confirms the boy has these powers even though the ברייתא in Step 18 left them out of his list.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: introduces a ruling of אמוראים that supports what was just said
He has, meaning the act has legal force when he does it

phrases.english: It was also stated:
רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
He has a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: Meaning a גט he gives her counts and blocks his brothers.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי:
phrases.english: And similarly רב תחליפא בר אבימי said:
He has levirate betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 19 that the boy's מאמר has force.
steps.raayaObject: That a nine-year-old's מאמר (and גט) have legal force.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Rulings of שמואל (through רב יהודה) and of רב תחליפא בר אבימי.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי מאיר says the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: the boy has both a גט and a מאמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: he has a גט and he has a מאמר. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא that supports the אמוראים: רבי מאיר holds the boy has both גט and מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rulings of the אמוראים are backed by a תנא. But because the ruling is tied to רבי מאיר, the גמרא will next check whether this fits his other statements.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this: brings a ברייתא as support
These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: It is also taught so:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ גֵּט, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ מַאֲמָר,
phrases.english: He has a bill of divorce, and he has levirate betrothal,
the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא as further support for Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That a nine-year-old has a valid גט and a valid מאמר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really say the boy has a גט?
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר comparing the boy's חליצה to an adult's גט. If the boy had his own גט, רבי מאיר should have compared it to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really hold that the boy has a גט? A ברייתא teaches: they made a nine-year-old's ביאה like an adult's מאמר. רבי מאיר says: they made a nine-year-old's חליצה like an adult's גט. If the boy had a גט, רבי מאיר should have said 'like his own גט'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ruling in Step 21 by quoting a different statement of רבי מאיר that seems to show the boy has no real גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר describes the boy's חליצה by comparing it to an adult's גט. If the boy could give a working גט himself, the simpler comparison would be his own גט. Reaching for an adult's גט suggests the boy's own גט does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) made it like, meaning they gave it the same legal force as
And if it were so: introduces what the text should have said

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר יֵשׁ לוֹ גֵּט?
phrases.english: And does רבי מאיר hold he has a bill of divorce?
But isn't it taught:
They made the relations of a nine-year-old
like levirate betrothal of an adult,
רבי מאיר says:
They made the חליצה of a nine-year-old
like a bill of divorce of an adult.
And if it is so — let him teach: like his own bill of divorce!
phrases.notes: "His own" means the boy's own גט. Why compare to an adult if the boy has a גט himself?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר יֵשׁ לוֹ גֵּט? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of Step 21 using another statement of רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: That רבי מאיר holds a nine-year-old has a valid גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר compares the boy's חליצה to an adult's גט instead of to the boy's own גט. That suggests the boy has no גט of his own.

steps.title: The boy's גט counts, but it is weaker
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the boy does have a גט, but it is weaker than an adult's. That is why רבי מאיר compared the חליצה to an adult's גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: He has a גט, but it is a lesser one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the boy's גט is real, but it is weaker than an adult's, so it was not the right thing to compare to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements of רבי מאיר now fit together. The boy has a גט, as Step 21 says. But his חליצה has the force of a full adult's גט, which is stronger than the boy's own weaker גט, so רבי מאיר compared it to an adult's גט.
steps.whatToRemember: A nine-year-old יבם has מאמר and גט, but his acts are weaker than an adult's. His ביאה always blocks the brothers. His מאמר blocks only when it comes first. His גט counts but is weaker than an adult's גט.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said:
He has it, but it is lesser.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אִית לֵיהּ וְזוּטַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the boy's גט as real but weaker, which explains why רבי מאיר chose a different comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר compared to an adult's גט because the boy has no גט at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boy has a גט, but it is weaker. So the full-strength comparison had to be an adult's גט.

steps.title: According to רבן גמליאל, an adult's גט still works after a boy's גט
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that a second גט to the יבמה does nothing. But this is only when both brothers are the same kind (both adults or both boys). An adult's גט after a boy's גט does work, because the boy's גט is weaker.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבן גמליאל, who says there is no גט after a גט: that is only an adult after an adult, or a boy after a boy. But an adult after a boy does work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is spelling out what he meant in Step 23 when he said the boy's גט is weaker. He starts with the opinion of רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, for רבן גמליאל, once one brother gave the יבמה a גט, a second brother's גט adds nothing. Here we learn an exception: if the first גט came from a boy, it did not fully use up the power to give a גט, so an adult brother's גט afterward still counts. That shows the boy's גט is real but weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that after one brother gives the יבמה a גט, another brother's גט does nothing
There is no גט after a גט: a second brother's גט has no effect
This applies only..., which brings in a limit on a rule
An adult / a minor (here, the boy)

phrases.english: According to Rabban Gamliel, who said
there is no bill of divorce after a bill of divorce —
this applies only to an adult after an adult
and a minor after a minor,
but an adult after a minor — it is effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, דְּאָמַר אֵין גֵּט אַחַר גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's answer from Step 23 using רבן גמליאל's opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the boy's גט is real but weaker, inside the opinion of רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבן גמליאל, any first גט would block every later גט, so the boy's גט would be just like an adult's.
steps.terutzMaskana: A boy's גט does not block a later adult's גט, so it is weaker than an adult's גט.

steps.title: According to רבנן, a boy's גט does not work after an adult's גט
steps.stepSummary: רבנן hold that a second גט to the יבמה does take effect. But this is only when both brothers are the same kind. A boy's גט after an adult's גט does nothing, because the boy's גט is weaker.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, who say there is a גט after a גט: that is only an adult after an adult, or a boy after a boy. But a boy after an adult does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע now shows the same weakness of the boy's גט according to the other side, the רבנן. This finishes his explanation of why רבי מאיר compared the boy's חליצה to an adult's גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, for רבנן, a second brother's גט also takes effect. Here we learn an exception: a boy's גט cannot add anything after an adult's גט, because it is too weak. So according to both opinions, the boy's גט is real but less than an adult's.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue on רבן גמליאל
There is a גט after a גט: a second brother's גט does take effect
It does not work / it has no effect

steps.whatToRemember: The boy's גט is a real גט, but weaker than an adult's. According to רבן גמליאל, it cannot block an adult's later גט. According to רבנן, it cannot add anything after an adult's גט. This is why רבי מאיר compared the boy's חליצה to an adult's גט and not to the boy's own גט.
steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions show the weakness in opposite directions. For רבן גמליאל the case is an adult after a boy, which works. For רבנן the case is a boy after an adult, which does not work. Both cases teach the same idea: the boy's גט counts for less.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows Step 24 and gives the matching explanation for the רבנן's opinion, which completes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the boy's גט is real but weaker, inside the opinion of רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבנן, any second גט takes effect, so a boy's גט after an adult's גט would also count.
steps.terutzMaskana: A boy's גט adds nothing after an adult's גט. This confirms it is weaker and explains רבי מאיר's comparison of the boy's חליצה to an adult's גט.
